shots.vo: This is the deadliest job on Earth. And it's about catching... crab.
Welcome to the Bering Sea — Dutch Harbor, Alaska. Winter water: two degrees.
The tool: a 750-pound steel cage. Bait it with cod, and crabs crawl in — but can't crawl out.
Drop it a hundred meters deep. Wait two days. Haul it up — full... or empty.
One good trip pays a deckhand over ten thousand dollars. In five days.
The catch? Minus twenty, forty-foot waves, and ice that builds up until boats flip. This job kills at eighty times the average rate.
Then, in 2022 — ten billion snow crabs just... vanished. The season was canceled for the first time ever.
A marine heat wave had spiked their metabolism. There wasn't enough food. They starved. Follow for part two: the two-hundred-million-dollar ghost fleet.
